items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: And they sang on all the records I did with Lou Christie.

ctx.x: Speaking of “Lightnin’ Strikes,” this is from about two weeks ago, Lou Christie passed away. New York Times obituary and this – I’ll read a bit of it, a small bit. “February 1966 with ‘Lightnin’ Strikes’ chart topper marked by a sweeping arrangement by the producer Charles Calello featuring glimmering piano, ringing church bells, and radiant backing vocals from a vocal trio, The Delicates.” I think that’s really hip, that the New York Times mentioned the arranger.

Well we actually made that record at the piano. The group that we used were The Angels – Peggy Farina, they had the hit record, “My Boyfriend’s Back,” but we used them as background singers. And they sang on all the records I did with Lou Christie. And we would get together, because they didn’t read music, and we would work the record out around the piano. So before I would go into the studio I knew what the record was going to sound like. There was the one thing that I didn’t anticipate was the guitar solo. The…
orchestration. And the reason why I did it, as a producer I had the record made. If there was something somebody could bring to the table I wanted to have it.
